title: Company-wide policies and processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Alexandra Kim
content:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and cross-functional stakeholders. Owners are listed per section; exceptions must be raised to people-ops or the listed owner.

Scope and intent

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and temporary staff.
- Covers corporate cloud accounts, production and non-production systems, internal tools, third-party vendors, procurement processes, and travel/expense reimbursement.
- Objective: reduce risk, reduce ambiguity, and speed decision-making by standardizing approvals and operational runbooks.

Roles & responsibilities

- People Ops: policy owner and coordinator for access appeals, travel exceptions, and hiring-related permissions.
- Security: reviewer & enforcer for RBAC, data classification, and vendor security questionnaires.
- Finance & Legal: owner for procurement thresholds, contracts, and vendor payments.
- Engineering Managers: approve technical access requests and emergency changes for owned services.
- Service Owners: maintain runbooks, pre-approved change windows, and rollback plans.

1) Access & Permissions

Overview:
- Principle of least privilege (PoLP) by default; role-based access control (RBAC) used where available.
- All privileged access (production consoles, KMS/HSM keys, billing) requires justification and manager approval.

Process — requesting access:
1. Submit an access request via the Access Request form (Confluence template: "access-request-template") with: business justification, required scope (read/write/admin), and expected duration.
2. Manager approval (auto-approval for non-privileged tools) and service owner verification for production-level permissions.
3. Security review for elevated scopes (e.g., KMS, HSM, customer data stores).
4. Access issued with an expiration (default 90 days for elevated access), logged in the Access Audit Log (internal system: access-audit.redwood).

Periodic review:
- Quarterly role reviews by People Ops and Security.
- Any account with elevated privileges must have an owner and rotation schedule.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Documented in the service runbook. Temporary tokens issued via emergency-access.redwood with multi-party approval (on-call SRE + manager + security). Duration: 4 hours default.

2) Change Management

Goal: minimize disruption while enabling fast iteration.

Change categories:
- Standard (pre-approved, low-risk): routine infra updates, scheduled config changes.
- Normal (planned, medium risk): deploys that require a ticket, owner approval, and change window.
- Emergency (high risk, unplanned): production fixes that must follow the emergency change procedure.

Process for normal changes:
1. Create a change ticket in Jira (project: CHANGE). Include owner, roll-forward and rollback plan, risk assessment, monitoring plan, and start/end windows.
2. Peer review and service owner sign-off.
3. Schedule in the next available change window (see Change Window Calendar).
4. Post-deploy verification and update ticket with metrics (latency, error rate, rollout %, incidents).

Emergency change flow:
1. Triage and short-lived approval by on-call + service owner.
2. Implement change, monitor for 30 minutes.
3. Post-mortem and retro within 3 business days; update the change ticket and runbook.

Approval matrix (example):
| Change Type | Required Approvals | Max Lead Time | Owner |
|-------------|--------------------|---------------:|-------|
| Standard | Team lead | 0 days | Service owner |
| Normal (>=1 hour impact) | Service owner + Eng manager | 3 days | Service owner |
| Normal (>=4 hour impact) | Service owner + Eng manager + Platform | 7 days | Platform team |
| Emergency | On-call + Service owner | immediate | On-call owner |

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Weekly maintenance windows: Tue 02:00–04:00 UTC.
- Blackout: Last Friday of quarter and 24 hours before major releases.

3) Data Management

Principles:
- Classify data at creation and enforce handling rules: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Encrypt data at rest and in transit. Customer data tagged as Restricted by default.

Data classification summary:
| Classification | Examples | Retention | Encryption | Access Pattern |
|---------------|----------|----------|-----------|----------------|
| Public | Marketing materials | n/a | n/a | Open |
| Internal | Internal wikis, non-customer logs | 3 years | TLS | Team-level RBAC |
| Confidential | Payroll, contracts | 7 years | AES-256 at rest | Finance & HR only |
| Restricted | Customer PII, model training datasets with PII | per contract | AES-256 + KMS | Minimal, audited |

Data retention & deletion:
- Defaults set per system: logs (90 days), analytics (1 year), backups (90 days unless contracted). Exceptions must be filed with people-ops + legal.
- Data deletion requests: use the Data Deletion Request template; legal and security review required for customer data.

Data access audits and SLOs:
- Access audit logs retained for 1 year.
- Quarterly audit of all accounts with access to Restricted data.

Acceptable tooling and storage:
- Approved cloud buckets: s3.redwood-prod, s3.redwood-internal. Unapproved storage (personal drives, unmanaged cloud accounts) is prohibited for company data.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- <= $1,000: team lead approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: department head + finance notification.
- > $25,000: procurement team + legal review + finance approval.

Process for purchasing:
1. Complete the Purchase Request template in Confluence and attach vendor quote.
2. Submit to procurement@redwood.com (or via the procurement Jira board).
3. Procurement will review contracts and route to finance/legal if > $25k or if vendor stores customer data.
4. Once approved, procurement issues a purchase order (PO). All invoices must reference PO number.

Expense reimbursement:
- Employees file expenses in Expensify within 30 days with receipts. Approver = direct manager.
- Per diem rules: domestic travel meal cap $75/day, international $100/day unless pre-approved.
- Travel upgrades: allowed only with pre-approval for business-critical travel.

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Vendor completes Security Questionnaire (VSA template).
- Review by Security for data handling and encryption.
- Legal executes MSA or Data Processing Agreement where required.
- Finance sets payment terms and assigns GL codes.
- Operational contact and escalation path recorded in vendor record.

Ongoing monitoring:
- Quarterly vendor risk review for any vendor with access to Restricted or Confidential data.
- Annual security attestation requested for vendors classified as High risk.

Offboarding:
- Revoke all vendor access (accounts, API keys, SSO integrations).
- Verify data return or secure deletion per contract.

6) Travel Policy (summary)

Booking & approvals:
- All business travel must be booked through Concur (preferred) or with travel@redwood.com.
- Manager approval required for all trips. For travel >5 days or international, require director-level approval.

Safety & security:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must notify people-ops and security and register with the travel safety program.

Expenses and reimbursement:
- File within 30 days with itemized receipts. Non-itemized meals capped at $25 per meal without receipt.
- Personal expenses (alcohol, leisure upgrades) are not reimbursable unless pre-approved.

Emergency assistance:
- 24/7 travel assistance: +1-800-555-0100 (vendor TravelSafe). Contact people-ops concurrently.

7) Internal templates & forms (quick index)

- access-request-template (Confluence) — Use for all account and permission requests.
- purchase-request-template — Use for purchase approvals; attach quote and cost center.
- vendor-onboarding-checklist — Required for every new vendor.
- data-deletion-request — Required for any request to remove customer or Restricted data.
- change-request-template (Jira) — Use when submitting normal changes.
- travel-authorization-form — Use for director-level approvals.

Appendices

A. Exception & escalation process
- Exceptions to policy must be submitted using the Policy Exception form and include mitigation steps and a 30/60/90-day review plan.
- Escalation path: Service Owner -> Engineering Manager -> People Ops -> CISO -> CEO.

B. Contacts & owner directory
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com (Alexandra Kim)
- Security (RBAC & vendor reviews): security@redwood.com (Marcus Lee)
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.com (Priya Natarajan)
